newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Amcor to decide on under-performing units.
newsitem.headline: Amcor to decide on under-performing units.

text.p: Paper and packaging group Amcor Ltd said on Wednesday it would decide by the end of July on whether to sell some under-performing businesses.
The comprise include German box maker Holfelder, U.S. packaging group Cello Bag and U.S. paper marker McKinley Paper.

"We will have the 1997/98 budget for those businesses by the end of June and we would expect to make a decision one way or the other by the end of July," managing director Don Macfarlane told a Securities Institute luncheon.
Macfarlane said the Holfelder and McKinley businesses currently had a book value of over A$1 billion each.
He said Amcor had already written down the Holfelder business by A$40 million and that further writedowns in this business were expected when the company releases its results for the 1996/97 year.
He said it was not an ideal time to be selling these businesses as paper prices were near their bottom in the current cycle.

"The fact that we have already announced that we are going to make further writedowns is an indication that we might be selling these businesses for less than the amounts that we have paid for them," Macfarlane said.
He said Amcor could not afford to subsidise under-performing businesses, as the group faces a margin squeeze and declining profitability in the current year.

Last week, Amcor announced it expected profit for the six months ended June 30, 1997, to be lower than the year ago period and lower than the 1996/97 first half. It also said it expected significant writedowns in some assets in the 1996/97 year.
Amcor shares were trading at A$8.37 at 0500 GMT (3 p.m.) on Wednesday, down five cents on Tuesday's close.
